title: A build-floor rejection after its corrections releases the item unbumped: the retro's PASS is the last C1 entry and the rejection carries no code
summary: Cycle 1761 (wave 42) failed when the build handoff floor rejected the deliverable after 2 corrections. Its C1 record: build PASS with abort_reason 'review gate: phase "build" deliverable rejected after 2 correction(s)…' and no error code, then retro PASS as the last entry. cycleclassify reads only the last entry's error codes, so the failure is not task-level, FailureInputsFor marks it system-level, and the ledger shows 'cycle-failure-release' with failure_count unset: the item can be redrawn without ever reaching the quarantine ceiling. R1c (#724) fixed this class for the triage endings only. Nuance: 1761's own cause was an unsatisfiable TDD predicate (a pipeline/persona defect, #728), so whether the item or the pipeline pays should follow the correction's diagnosis, not the absence of a code.
fix: Record the build-floor rejection at C1 with a coded diagnostic (and read the failing phase's entry, not the retro's, when classifying); decide task- vs system-level from the rejection's cause (a TDD-owned predicate defect is the pipeline's; a build that cannot meet a satisfiable contract is the item's).
acceptance: A 1761-shaped workspace (build floor rejected after corrections, retro last) classifies from the build's coded entry, not the retro's PASS (red today)
The item is bumped when the build could not meet a satisfiable contract, and not when the predicate was defective
